about: Measured rows (felizjueves.measured): what one device toolchain reported about one emitted translation unit on one card, keyed on device.MeasuredKey(spec, arch, toolchain).key(). Observations of a toolchain, not claims about this code. NOT comparable to [JEngine, v2, Table 4]: their kernels, their compiler, their A100.

header.what: Measured rows: what a device toolchain reported about one emitted translation unit (felizjueves.measured).
header.key: Rows are keyed on felizjueves.device.MeasuredKey(spec, arch, toolchain).key() -- the generation Spec, the card's Arch, the compiler as it reports itself (#37).
header.nature: Observations of a toolchain, not claims about this code: a compiler bump moving a number is news about the compiler.
header.not_compared: Nothing here is compared against [JEngine, v2, Table 4] (their kernels, compiler and A100); see data/literature/jengine/README.md.
header.units: nvcc: registers per thread, spill BYTES (ptxas -v). hipcc: VGPRs per lane, spilled REGISTER COUNTS (VGPR + SGPR; no store/load split, so both spill fields carry it). See each row's spill_unit and raw.
header.remeasure: PYTHONPATH=src uv run python -m felizjueves.measured --remeasure --backend both
header.wallclock: runtime_ns is the MEDIAN host wall-clock of a cell's whole batched launch sequence (every build_pq_kernels batch into one zeroed J, then a synchronize), over `repeats` timed sequences after a warm-up, on a wide-T input; spread_ns is their interquartile range; raw 'wallclock:*' has the rest, and 'wallclock:near:*' the same on a near-T input. Taken alone on an uncontended box by test/test_kernel_device.py's opt-in wall-clock sweep (FJ_WALLCLOCK_STORE). Compare only within one arch, across n_batches -- never across vendors.
header.gpu_util: #93: every row with runtime_ns carries raw 'wallclock:gpu_util_before' / '_after' and 'wallclock:near:gpu_util_before' / '_after' (and, on a lever row timed after #93, 'wallclock:control:...' likewise): the card's utilisation in percent from its own SMI, as the sweep's gate let the input through and 1 s after its last timed sequence (one read discarded first: rocm-smi's first read after a pause averages over it, i.e. over our own run). null means UNKNOWN, never idle: the .../recycle@... rows were timed before #93 and record null (their sm_86 rows keep #55's 'wallclock:gpu_util_pct_before_max', the highest settled reading over the cell's four timed inputs). The 40 literal SUBGRID rows were re-timed behind the gate by #93, one session per arch.
header.levers: #55: rows keyed .../recycle@... are the recycle arm (lower.recycle, measured.lever_cells) of every SUBGRID cell, timed against a same-session literal control kept in their raw 'wallclock:control:*'; measured.lever_ab is the verdict. CONCLUSION: recycle stays opt-in. nvcc 13.0 and hipcc / ROCm 7.2.4 emit IDENTICAL machine code for the two arms in every batch kernel of every cell (both scalarise the statically indexed slot array), registers and spills match exactly, and the clock is NEUTRAL at every cell on sm_86; on gfx1200 the declared rule reads 4 cells at L <= 10 as SLOWER, on that identical code -- the A/B's noise floor, not the lever.
header.asym: #113: rows keyed .../b<n>/j/asym@... are the asymmetric-split STUDY (felizjueves.asym; its docstring is the rule, committed before any such row existed): L in {13, 16} x n_batches in {4, 5, 7, 8}, a batch list Spec and partition refuse, each timed against its two nearest legal neighbours in the same session (raw 'wallclock:control:b<n>:*'; no literal row re-timed). A phase the card was taken during was discarded and retaken (raw 'wallclock:gate_discarded_phases'). CONCLUSION: every cell is WORSE than its best legal neighbour on both sm_86 and gfx1200, so jengine/symmetry-breaking-splits-are-worse is asserted.
header.counters: #110: fp64_flops, dram_bytes_read, dram_bytes_written and counter_ns are the card's own performance counters as a profiler reported them for one kernel -- ncu on NVIDIA (fp64_flops = dadd + dmul + 2 x dfma thread instructions; DRAM bytes at sector granularity), rocprofv3's counter mode on AMD (GL2C <-> EA bytes, an upper bound on DRAM; gfx1200 has no fp64 counter, so fp64_flops is None there) -- with the profiler in counter_tool, the vendor meaning in counter_unit, the invocation in command and every counter by its exact name in raw. counter_ns is the kernel's duration under counter collection (serialised, replayed): NOT a timing, never runtime_ns. The counts are canonical; arithmetic_intensity and achieved_flops_per_s are derived, never stored. Units: fp64_flops: fp64 floating-point operations executed (FMA = 2); dram_bytes_read: bytes (vendor meaning: the row's counter_unit); dram_bytes_written: bytes (vendor meaning: the row's counter_unit); counter_ns: ns, the profiler's kernel duration under counter collection -- NOT a timing; arithmetic_intensity: FLOP / byte = fp64_flops / (dram_bytes_read + dram_bytes_written), derived; achieved_flops_per_s: FLOP / s = fp64_flops / counter_ns, derived. Counter rows live in data/measured/roofline.json, ONE PER BATCH KERNEL, keyed MeasuredKey.key() + '#<batch>' (plan order, from 0); a cell's counters are their sum, derived (measured_store.cell_counters), never stored. NOT comparable to [JEngine, v2, Fig. 7]: their kernels, their A100.
header.f: #278: rows keyed .../b1/f/literal@... are the fused Fock build of [Fock] §3 on the HGP recurrence (milestone 12), one row per (class, arch, toolchain): the class (la,lb|lc,ld) in AO order -- NOT the K rows' Hermite pairing -- over the 21-class ladder, every shell l <= 2, one batch, no lever. Units as above: each row's spill_unit and raw say which (spill bytes on nvcc, spilled register counts on hipcc); compare within one arch only. A timed F row carries every 'wallclock:*gpu_util_*' key as a reading, never null. Written by #288's measurement: the compile side by python -m felizjueves.measured --remeasure --target f --L 0 1 2, the clock by test/test_fock_ondevice.py's opt-in sweep (FJ_WALLCLOCK_F=1, behind the gate; its docstring is the protocol: one off-diagonal launch of 2048 x 128 contracted quartets, runtime_ns on the wide input, wallclock:near:* on the near one); nothing here is compared against [Fock]'s A100 timings, and there is no published register table for its §3.2 kernel.
